attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his Substack post, published under his name and not quoting anyone else.

semantics.note: The normalised claim keeps 'it appears', 'at present', and both separate scopes. It is a hedged observation about the present: 'it appears' frames a tentative impression, not a firm assertion.

contract.note: The contract correctly treats 'It appears' as covering the whole statement and declines the plain-reading exception, which applies only to firm language. 'Most or all' and 'much closer' are undefined, so no fair binary test exists.

reviews.rationale: This is a tentative impression, flagged by 'It appears', with no defined population or comparison measure. Under the policy, hedged language is not scored. The packet lists no evidence items (two sources were read but not used), and nothing in it bears on scoring. Not adjudicable.
